A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the notion of argumenthood plays an important role in the interpretation of prepositional phrases, and that the distinction between arguments vs. adjuncts is not only useful to disambiguate the attachment site but also the nature of the preposition.
the problem of PP attachment can be solved as a four-way classification problem, with the best results being obtained if the classification is performed in two steps.
, in order to reach an accurate identification of the attachment of PPs, it is crucial to take into account both the site of the PP attachment and the nature of attachment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the distinction between arguments (which are obligatory and semantically constrained) and adjuncts (which are optional and semantically unconstrained) is a crucial factor in determining the attachment of prepositional phrases.
the notion of argument is crucial in the interpretation of PPs, and that it is useful to distinguish between the two aspects of arguments: the site of attachment and the nature of attachment.
the problem of PP attachment is not only a problem of choosing the attachment site, but also one of choosing the nature of the relation of the attachment site with the rest of the sentence.
